html:
A law passed on 21 April 1649 by the assembly of the colony of Maryland, granting freedom of worship to all Christians who believed in the Trinity. It was one of the first laws in the Americas to guarantee religious toleration.

Maryland was founded in 1634 by the Calvert family, the Lords Baltimore, as a haven for English Catholics, who faced penalties at home. But Protestants soon outnumbered Catholics there, and England itself was in the hands of the Puritans during the English Civil War. The act was a way to protect the Catholic minority by protecting everyone.

Its limits were sharp. Anyone who denied the Trinity or Jesus could be put to death, and insulting the Virgin Mary or the saints was punished. Jews and non-Christians had no protection. The Puritans who took over Maryland repealed the act in 1654; it came back later and was finally ended in 1692, when the Church of England became the colony's official church. Its spirit later shaped the religious freedom of the United States.
sum: A law passed on 21 April 1649 by the assembly of the colony of Maryland, granting freedom of worship to all Christians who believed in the Trinity. It was one of the first laws in the Americas to guarantee religious toleration.
